Looking at the previous attempt, I output the Markdown *embed* instead of the actual `.fd` source — the validator correctly rejected that, since a `.fd` file must start with the spec provenance comment and `figdown 0.1 <genre>` line, not a Markdown image/embed. Here is the corrected `.fd` source itself.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Alert-forwarding chain"

block probe "Probe" "emits raw samples"
block normalizer "Normalizer" "reshapes samples"
block sink "Sink" "writes to storage"

edge probe -> normalizer via=(60,20),(90,40)
edge normalizer -> sink
```

To embed this in the host Markdown document (after building `alert-forwarding-chain.svg` from this source), use:

```markdown
![Alert-forwarding chain: probe feeds normalizer, which feeds sink](figures/alert-forwarding-chain.svg)

<sub>source: [figures/alert-forwarding-chain.fd](figures/alert-forwarding-chain.fd)</sub>
```

Notes:
- The `via=(60,20),(90,40)` waypoint list on the `probe -> normalizer` edge is the explicit routing you asked for, so that connector jogs through those two points instead of drawing straight — leaving room for the future element between probe and normalizer.
- `normalizer -> sink` is left unrouted (straight), since nothing was asked to route it around.
- Labels are kept short per the block genre's guidance — the surrounding prose (probe = raw samples, normalizer = reshaping, sink = storage) carries the detail, the figure just carries structure.

Run `node <skill-dir>/build-svg.js alert-forwarding-chain.fd` to render and confirm `OK`, then look at the render before calling this done.
